item.title: Banak high school celebrates historic first Grade 10 graduation
item.description: The 59-pioneer grade 10 students of Banak high school in Boikin LLG, Wewak district (Supplied) Banak Junior High School in Boikin Local-Level Government (LLG), Wewak district, marked a milestone on tuesday with its first Grade 10 graduation where fifty-nine students graduated as the school's pioneer class.
item.content:encoded:
The 59-pioneer grade 10 students of Banak high school in Boikin LLG, Wewak district (Supplied)

Banak Junior High School in Boikin Local-Level Government (LLG), Wewak district, marked a milestone on tuesday with its first Grade 10 graduation where fifty-nine students graduated as the school's pioneer class.

The occassion, held under the theme, "Celebrating Achievements, Inspiring the future", brought together locals from neighboring villages in both Boikin and Dagua LLG to celebrate the establishment and growth of Boikin LLG's newest high school. Otto Sauiembi, a long-serving Board Chairman of the school, applauded the students for setting the legacy of the school.

"Thank you for making us proud", he said.

Joining him to congratulate the pioneer class, keynote speaker and Wewak District's Primary School Inspector Vincent Illowen also shared similar remarks. "Beat the garamut! Banak has a high school that is here to stay", Illowen said.

During his keynote speech, he challenged the teachers to produce exceptional students as Banak High School has the potential of creating quality education.

Illowen was acknowledged by Sauiembi and the pioneer principal of the school, Richard Kaus, for getting this new school registered.

Banak Junior High School's success was also alluded to the pioneer head teacher, Richard Kaus.

A representative from the Education Division of East Sepik Raphael Borungai, applauded Kaus for taking on the challenge in bringing up the new school.

He said Kaus also set a similar record at the current Moem Junior High School in Wewak.

This milestone occasion for the people of Boikin and Dagua LLG, shows the strong support and collaboration between staff, students and the locals.

item.title: Catholic Church calls for online child protection
item.description: Fr John Joseph of the Catholic Diocese of Lae (Supplied) The Catholic Church is calling for stronger protection of children and young people from harmful online content, saying parents, churches and schools must play a greater role in guiding them.
item.content:encoded:
Fr John Joseph of the Catholic Diocese of Lae (Supplied)

The Catholic Church is calling for stronger protection of children and young people from harmful online content, saying parents, churches and schools must play a greater role in guiding them.

Fr John Joseph of the Catholic Diocese of Lae raised the concern during the National Censorship Policy Workshop in Lae, where discussions focused on protecting children and young people in the digital space.

Fr Joseph says children as young as seven and eight years old are already exposed to inappropriate material online.

He says the church places strong emphasis on the formation of children and young people to help them develop positive values and make responsible choices.

The church's approach focuses on religious education and guiding young people through Christian teachings.

Fr Joseph says the church believes in strengthening children's understanding of Gospel values as they grow up in a changing digital environment.

He says protecting children from harmful online content requires a shared effort involving parents, churches, schools, communities and government agencies.

The call comes as Papua New Guinea continues discussions on strengthening censorship measures and addressing the risks children face when accessing online platforms.

item.title: Preparation begins for 36th Lutheran Synod in 2028

Francis Ambuk-represents History and Pr Reina Kubong-represents future church (NBC News) A groundbreaking was held recently in Madang, marking the commencement of preparatory work by the Lutheran Church in the provinc
item.content:encoded:
(L-R) Rev Lukas Kedabing-Assistant Bishop, Rev Bon Nelson-Madang District President, Ramsey Pariwa-Madang Governor & Synod Patron, Daniel Aloi-Synod Planning committee Chairman, Rev. Francis Ambuk-represents History and Pr Reina Kubong-represents future church (NBC News)

A groundbreaking was held recently in Madang, marking the commencement of preparatory work by the Lutheran Church in the province towards hosting the Church's 36th National Synod in January 2028.

The ceremony was held at Nagada Plantation, an old plantation owned by the Lutheran Church, towards the north coast.

Nagada will be the central location or site for the 2028 Synod.

Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa and Provincial Administrator, Daniel Aloi, were joined by senior clergymen from the church; Rev. Lucas Kedabing, Assistant Bishop of ELC- PNG, Rev. Bon Nelson - District President of Madang, Pastor Francis Ambuk, representing older pastors in Madang and Pastor Reiner Kubong, representing younger pastors, in the ceremony.

The event was witnessed by the General Secretary of ELC- PNG, Bernard Kaisum, Lutheran faithfuls, and the general public.

Mr Kaisum emphasised the importance of the upcoming synod, stating it will be the first for the next 50 years; both in the Church's calendar and the country's journey after independence.

The groundbreaking was followed by the unveiling of a huge billboard at the Nagada Junction, which declares that the next 50 years for ELC- PNG begins at Nagada, which will be the site of the 2028 Synod.

He also expressed gratitude to the local working committee, headed by Chairman and Madang's Provincial Administrator, Daniel Aloi; for starting the ground work early.

"People of Madang, you must be prepared for the Synod. As host, we must prepare the groundwork. It's gonna be a lot of hard work, but we must work with absolute faith in God that we can do it.

"We, from the headquarters; are happy to see those of you who have come to witness this special occasion. You represent the thousands of Lutheran faithfuls in this province who can not make it here to witness this event.

"The Synod will test our transport systems, and our ability to host such big event so we must be well prepared," Mr Kaisum said.

Chairman of the local organising committee and Madang's Provincial Administrator, Daniel Aloi, said it's a long road ahead for the committee.

"We have come this far with no political or business support. This is only one part of the Synod, and I can't think of any other way to do this but to continue to pray. What we are doing is like what John the Baptist did; preparing the groundwork for the Synod.

"We report to the Madang District Council, and we all must have a responsibility in this," he said.

Mr Aloi added that the committee is going ahead with the preparation despite critics from certain people that Madang is not ready to host the Synod.

Governor Ramsey Pariwa, meanwhile, was not happy that it has taken a long time for the groundwork to begin.

"It's been nine months since the last Synod ended in Siassi, Morobe Province and we brought the Synod shield to Madang. I am not happy that it took us this long to make decisions and start working. We have delayed work by nine months, and we cannot afford to waste any more time. It's time to work," Governor Pariwa stated.

He added that God has a plan for Madang, and the people must be ready to receive what He has to give.

Pariwa said, "Madang has not hosted a Synod in many years. We have been roaming in the wilderness, indulging ourselves in too many ungodly things like killing and cutting; and law, and order has deteriorated.

"We have played too much Church politics, and this must stop now. God wants to visit us, and we can't stop Him. Church politics has destroyed the church. Put your differences aside, and start working together. We are not here to please anybody. This is God's business."

Governor Pariwa is the Patron of the 36th Lutheran Synod.

item.title: EHP Provincial Government releases K2.5 million in food relief assistance
item.description: Eastern Highlands Deputy Governor Kenia Kakavu (second from left), Disaster Coordinator Benjamin Danny (centre) and Deputy Provincial Administrator Michael Mogia (third from right) with LLG Presidents (NBC News) Twenty-five Local Level Government (LLG) Presidents in Eastern Highlands Province will each receive K100,000 worth of food supplies to distribute to wards within their respective LLGs as c
item.content:encoded:
Eastern Highlands Deputy Governor Kenia Kakavu (second from left), Disaster Coordinator Benjamin Danny (centre) and Deputy Provincial Administrator Michael Mogia (third from right) with LLG Presidents (NBC News)

Twenty-five Local Level Government (LLG) Presidents in Eastern Highlands Province will each receive K100,000 worth of food supplies to distribute to wards within their respective LLGs as communities continue to feel the effects of El Niño.

Several LLG Presidents witnessed the presentation at Bintangor Wholesale and received updates on the assistance. Provincial Disaster Coordinator Benjamin Danny told the media that the K2.5 million in Provincial Government assistance is separate from the El Niño relief funding allocated by the National Government.

“The Provincial Executive Council has endorsed a K2.5 million from the Provincial Government’s 709 Internal Revenue Account for the first rollout of assistance.

The funding has now been made available for all LLG Presidents to distribute food supplies to wards within their respective LLGs,” Danny said.

He adds that the Provincial Government is working to access the additional K2.5 million in El Niño relief funding from the National Government to support the districts.

“Whatever we are providing now is funded by the Provincial Government as part of the first rollout. While this distribution is underway, we will draw down the funds from the National Government and continue the assistance to all respective wards,” he said.

Danny says the National Government funding will complement the Provincial Government’s efforts and is calling on District Development Authorities (DDAs) across the eight districts to provide additional support, as the current allocation to each LLG is insufficient.

He emphasized that the assistance is intended to provide food and water to communities affected by El Niño.

Meanwhile, Eastern Highlands Deputy Governor Kenia Kakavu, speaking on behalf of the LLG Presidents, thanked the Provincial Government for the timely assistance, saying it would help communities cope with the ongoing El Niño crisis.

item.title: Kumulgo family donates K50, 000 worth of food to Mian tribe in Gumine district
item.description: Stacks of rice, sugar and cartons of cooking oil donated by the Kumulgo family of the Nigi Marme Clan, worth more than K50,000, ready for distribution to the four wards of the Mian tribe. (Supplied) For the Mian Tribe of Gumine District in Simbu, it has been a week of double blessing.
item.content:encoded:
Stacks of rice, sugar and cartons of cooking oil donated by the Kumulgo family of the Nigi Marme Clan, worth more than K50,000, ready for distribution to the four wards of the Mian tribe. (Supplied)

For the Mian Tribe of Gumine District in Simbu, it has been a week of double blessing.

After receiving support from the Mian Elites Union earlier in the week, the tribe has now received more than K50,000 worth of El Niño relief supplies, rice, cooking oil and sugar from the Kumulgo family of the Nigi Marme Clan.

The supplies will support families in Wards 9, 10, 11 and 12 at Gumine Station, at a time when many families are struggling to secure basic food.

But for the family behind the donation, this is not a new story. It is a family story.

Leading the donation is John Bal, Director of Goroka Didiman Hardware, together with his wife, Theresa Bal, and their son, Jobby Bal, Director of FSEC Hire Cars and Security Services.

John Bal remembers doing the same thing in 1997, when Papua New Guinea faced a similar drought and food shortage. He delivered bags of rice to support communities then.

Nearly 30 years later, he is doing it again, this time with his son beside him.

"I am happy and blessed to see my son following in my footsteps. Generosity should not be a one-time thing. It must be passed from one generation to another." He said.

His son, Jobby Bal, said serving the community has always been part of his life, and should not be judged through politics.

"Community service is not new to me. I have always helped where I can," Mr Bal said.

He pointed to his previous work in Gumine, including the construction of the Gumine Market House, upgrading the Gumine League Field, supporting youth in sports, and assisting students and schools.

"Too often, people who genuinely want to help are overlooked, or their help is judged through political affiliations. Community service should be recognised for what it is a genuine commitment to improving people's lives," he said.

Mian tribal leaders and clan members thanked both the Kumulgo family and the Mian Elites Union for remembering their people during difficult times.

Speaking on behalf of the women Magret Kumai said the donation had brought relief to mothers who have been struggling to feed their families.

"On behalf of all the mothers of Mian, we thank the Kumulgo family. When there is no food in the house, it is the mothers who feel it first. This rice, oil and sugar will help our families for now, and we are truly grateful," Ms Kumai said.

"We are double blessed. First from our elites, and now from our own family. We thank them for not forgetting us."

Paul Kumam speaking on behalf of the men said the donation had strengthened unity and trust within the tribe.

"We thank Bal family for this big help. They have shown that when our own sons succeed, they come back to help the tribe. This is not about politics. This is about family and community. We will make sure this food reaches the four wards fairly — Wards 9, 10, 11 and 12." He said.

Mr Kuman said the two donations have sent a clear message across Gumine: development and community welfare is not the responsibility of government alone. Individuals, families, business leaders and community elites all have a role to play.

For the Mian people, the rice, oil and sugar will provide immediate relief.

But for John Bal, the real blessing was watching his son carry on the family legacy.

item.title: Magarima Station to access clean water
item.description: Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu left with helmet, Governor Philip Undialu (white button shirt) and Magarima Secondary School staff and community leaders celebrating the successful borehole drilling at the school yesterday (NBC News) Magarima Station in Hela Province is set to gain reliable access to clean water following the successful completion of a water borehole drilling project at Ma
item.content:encoded:
Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu left with helmet, Governor Philip Undialu (white button shirt) and Magarima Secondary School staff and community leaders celebrating the successful borehole drilling at the school yesterday (NBC News)

Magarima Station in Hela Province is set to gain reliable access to clean water following the successful completion of a water borehole drilling project at Magarima Secondary School.

​Hela Governor Philip Undialu confirmed the development, noting that the provincial government invested between K250,000 and K450,000 to complete the drilling at the school. The school will act as the primary custodian of the facility, ensuring both students and nearby communities benefit from the supply.

​The initiative is part of a broader K5 million provincial program targeting several key sites across the province. Magarima Secondary School represents the fourth successful site, joining Tari Hospital, Komo Secondary School, and the Koroba Catholic Church.

​"Access to clean water is a fundamental human right," Governor Undialu stated. "While this response directly addresses the challenges brought on by the El Niño drought, our objective is to provide a sustainable, long-term solution that serves our communities well beyond the current crisis."

​In addition to provincial funding, community development partner Hides Gas Gigira Limited (HGGL) has stepped up support. HGGL initially added K7 million to the province’s K5 million budget and has committed an additional K15 million—bringing total combined funding to K27 million.

He said the ​Hela Provincial Government will be looking at 11 borehole sites while Hides Gas Gigira Limited is 15 borehole sites.

​To complement the borehole program, Governor Undialu announced the distribution of 2,200 commercial-grade water purifiers across local-level government (LLG) wards, with each ward slated to receive 3 to 4 units. Magarima Secondary School is scheduled to receive 4 purifiers next week, capable of producing approximately eight cartons of bottled drinking water daily.

item.title: Lelang takes over from Ling-Stuckey as Treasurer
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has announced a cabinet reshuffle, ahead of the 2027 National Budget, and the 2027 National Election. Mr Marape in a statement released this afternoon says that he has appointed Joseph Lelang as the new Treasury Minister and moved Ian Ling Stuckey to the Ministry of Rural and Economic Development.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has announced a cabinet reshuffle, ahead of the 2027 National Budget, and the 2027 National Election.

Mr Marape in a statement released this afternoon says that he has appointed Joseph Lelang as the new Treasury Minister and moved Ian Ling Stuckey to the Ministry of Rural and Economic Development.

The Prime Minister says Mr Lelang’s appointment as Treasurer is a positive move, citing his background as an economist and his previous experience as head of the National Planning Department during his career in the public service

He said that this will relieve Mr. Ling Stuckey of the heavy pressures of Treasury, thus giving him more time to focus on his health, family and his people of Kavieng District.

Mr. Marape also says that Mr. Lelang’s immediate tasks will be to end borrowing of new loans, boost foreign direct investments into new resource projects, undertake a tax reforms, and strengthen Treasury’s role.

Mr. Ling Stuckey’s roles will see him oversee rural development strategies, economic modelling, price control, National Economic and Fiscal Commission, and labour mobility programmes.

Prime Minister Marape also adds that the country’s economy, grew from 79 billion kina to 160 billion kina under Ian Ling Stuckey’s watch over seven years, beginning in 2019.
